mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue their recent week-on-week recovery, weekday customer flows will rise and RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks. The signal fails if commuting proxies flatten or reverse, because retail visits depend on sustained return-to-work movement.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -38.6 to -24.9 and TRANSIT from -51.9 to -37.0 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain above their t-3w levels for at least two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in RESIDENTIAL time, paired with less PARKS substitution, will shift time back into outside-home errands and shopping, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week. The mechanism fails if stay-at-home intensity stops falling, because the retail gain depends on households spending less time at home.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed elevated at 20.7, 16.7, 13.7, 13.6 while PARKS remained below baseline except for a temporary rebound
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 7 days even though RESIDENTIAL falls and PARKS stays below its t-1w level.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline or improves, routine essential trips normalize first and spill over into nearby retail and recreation visits over a two-week lag. If grocery mobility drops again, the retail spillover weakens and the hypothesis fails.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2 points from baseline for two straight weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -6.0 to -1.0 before slipping to -5.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -2 and stays there for two weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT weakens relative to WORKPLACES, commuting becomes more constrained and discretionary retail falls with it over the next four weeks. The mechanism is rejected if transit mobility rebounds faster than workplaces, because the retail drag comes from suppressed access rather than weak labor activity alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below WORKPLACES by at least 10 points for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed far below WORKPLACES in every week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days while TRANSIT stays at least 10 points below WORKPLACES for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed PARKS rebound signals better weather and more out-of-home leisure, which pulls households back into adjacent shopping districts and raises RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks. The effect fails if park visits remain volatile or reverse, because the leisure signal would not be sustained.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points from the prior weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -21.3 to -11.6 and then to -6.4 before dropping to -24.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher within 14 days after a 10-point weekly rise in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stops declining and stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain depressed, households substitute toward home-based routines and avoid discretionary retail, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks. The signal fails if home time falls again or workplace mobility jumps, because the mechanism depends on persistent domestic substitution.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 12 points while WORKPLACES stays below -20 points for four weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained positive while WORKPLACES stayed deeply negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 12 and WORKPLACES staying below -20 for the whole window.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lag retail rebound follows simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES only after mobility restrictions ease enough for both commuting and shopping trips to expand together. The mechanism fails if only one of the two series improves, because the retail lift requires joint access and labor mobility.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:both commuting proxies improved from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Because RETAIL_REC is still near its recent lows despite improvements in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, the next four weeks will remain below the prior four-week average unless grocery and park activity also recover. The mechanism fails if retail rises without a broad-based rebound in these supporting trip types.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved only modestly from -51.0 to -33.9 while other mobility series also remained negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last-28-day mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not recover further and GROCERY_PHARM stays near current levels.
